lines.text: Sabine's letter was short. It always was, when she wanted something.
Lord Lucan. My son and daughter are still the Grand Measurer's guests at the Order's College. Bring them out with your father. My boats will wait at the river door. Consider it my favour. Sabine.
She had sent the same letter to Wren, at sea, on a ship nobody was supposed to know had sailed. With Sabine, you never want to know how.
I couldn't go with them. But I could feel them: four threads stretching south, thinner every day, down the coast and up the river into Aldcrown.
Wren told me later that it snowed in Aldcrown that midwinter, for the first time in living memory. People stood in the streets catching it on their tongues, and were afraid.
Mirelle's river door was a rusted iron gate under the palace wall, half under water, behind a curtain of ivy. At dawn on midwinter day, it was open.
You came. I wasn't sure anyone would.
You still talk too much before a fight.
Left shoulder.
...Is fine.
Tamsin went first, alone, in her old junior Measurer's robes, to the College where she had trained. She walked in by the front door. Nobody stopped her.
Junior Measurer Reed, with an urgent message for the Grand Measurer's young guests. From their mother.
Ilse put on her square spectacles again. She said they were for luck. I think she just liked them.
Oswin went to the Lowmarket. The Order had burned half of it after we left. The other half was waiting for him.
Tell the lord with the goat face we're ready.
And Wren climbed the bell tower of the Cathedral of the Seven in the snow, and lay flat beside the biggest bell to wait.
At noon the Square of the Seven was full. Every guild, every lord, every Lowmarket family the Order could herd there. Vance wanted the city to see.
No one has come for you, Lord Varr. Your son has chosen his kingdom over his father. I can't say I blame him.
Good. I raised him to be cleverer than me. It seems to have worked.
They led my father up the scaffold steps in Order chains, snow falling on his grey hair. He didn't look up at the bell tower. He had no reason to.
Half a kingdom away, on the wall at Greyhollow, I felt Wren's thread go still and cold and steady, the way it does just before she lets go.
Wren drew.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and thirty-one, coming soon.
